builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Learning to Bound: Monotonic, Calibrated Neural Upper Bounds for MPE Inference
summary: The method replaces classical bound computation for branch-and-bound MPE search, such as Mini-Bucket Elimination, with an amortized neural predictor whose admissibility comes from statistical calibration and whose monotonic tightening is enforced architecturally. It costs an offline training pipeline: generating solved or bounded MPE instances as training data, training the predictor, and validating calibration, plus the added system complexity of embedding a learned model inside the search loop. It can fail through distribution shift between training and deployment PGM instances, miscalibrated bounds that break admissibility and silently prune the true optimum, and workloads where classical bounds are already cheap enough that amortization yields no benefit.
rationale: This targets probabilistic graphical model inference rather than LLM or agent workloads, so it is only actionable if the reader's production system performs MPE search with branch-and-bound, which is a narrow specialty outside typical constrained-infrastructure ML engineering.
technique: Learned calibrated neural bounds for MPE search

claims.statement: The method replaces classical bound computation for branch-and-bound MPE search, such as Mini-Bucket Elimination, with an amortized neural predictor whose admissibility comes from statistical calibration and whose monotonic tightening is enforced architecturally. It costs an offline training pipeline: generating solved or bounded MPE instances as training data, training the predictor, and validating calibration, plus the added system complexity of embedding a learned model inside the search loop. It can fail through distribution shift between training and deployment PGM instances, miscalibrated bounds that break admissibility and silently prune the true optimum, and workloads where classical bounds are already cheap enough that amortization yields no benefit.

L2B delivers tighter, monotonic bounds at orders-of-magnitude lower cost than classical bound computation on every tested PGM family, with measurable improvements when integrated with branch-and-bound on high-treewidth instances; no single numeric factor is given.
